notes.content_summary: The document claims that the relevant category is described by a profinite fundamental group extending G by the ordinary fundamental group of Z, subject to a connectedness restriction; it then discusses removal of normality assumptions, full faithfulness of the quotient construction, reduction to a principal covering and descent. The second paragraph introduces infinitely many or locally defined ramification models, including Kummer divisors, and a compatibility condition between local models. These are document claims, not verified theorems in this run.
notes.scope_and_method: Only the assigned brief, meta.json, C.tex, H.tex, C_prior_questions.md, notation_snapshot.md, PREAMBLE.tex, the whole image, its two supplied halves and my own crops were accessed. No other reader or page, OCR, text extraction, external text, internet or proof source was used. All ordinary text and every inline formula were compared with both drafts. Whole and each half were viewed exactly once. Thirteen local crops were made and each viewed once; none was recropped.
notes.line_numbering: Physical main lines are counted from as developped as line 1 to than the restriction as line 27. Inserted lines are not counted. This makes twp, part of line 20, even though the prior C table calls it line 21. All bbox coordinates refer to the original 1679 x 2145 whole image, not to resized crops.

notes.mathematical_considerations_affecting_in: The functor language led me to inspect the interval between Z-prime and Z-prime/G, and the local compatibility language led me to inspect the interval between U and V. Both intervals are blank in the image; the expected mapsto and intersection were not supplied. All other formula choices were based on visible alphabet, position, primes and indices. No claim was evaluated as a theorem.
notes.comparison_conventions: Macro-only equivalences, including H struck versus deleted and H emph versus the observed underline, are not differences. Marked_in_H is yes where H explicitly marks the relevant locus with struck or ill; the evidence states when that mark covers deletion rather than letter uncertainty. It is no when corresponding text is unmarked, and absent for omitted ink. Uncertainty additions/removals are recorded as differences because they change the diplomatic reading.
